what: Does a coding agent add again an extra that a reviewer answered `remove` on an earlier merge request, when it can read the project's answer log, compared with when it cannot? Written and committed before any agent run.
why: Round 16 expert judge: no tool found feeds a reviewer's per-extra answers back to the coding agent; this tests whether doing so changes what the agent writes.

subject.agent: Claude Sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5) as a Claude Code subagent with file and shell tools, one fresh agent per run, no memory between runs
subject.prompt: eval/agent_log/prompt.md, word for word, with {REPO}, {TITLE} and {BODY} filled in; the same text in every arm

fixtures.written_by: the entrant, for this test; several issues invite a new package, and that is the same in both arms

issues.history: 5 per project, run once each with no answer log
issues.test: 10 per project, each run twice: once with the answer log in the repository, once without

answer_log.how: after the history runs, Itemator's rules (itemator/extras.py, rules v6 unchanged) list the extras of each history run against its issue; every extra is recorded as answered `remove`, in the shape of the published answer log, at .itemator/answers.json
answer_log.who: the entrant, standing in for a reviewer who answers `remove` to every extra; no real reviewer took part. This is said wherever the result is quoted.
answer_log.per_project: each project's log holds only its own history

arms.with: the project's answer log is in the repository at .itemator/answers.json
arms.without: no answer log; the prompt is the same, so it names a file that is not there

order: history runs first (textkit, then fetchit); then for each test issue in file order both arms, the with arm first on odd-numbered issues and the without arm first on even-numbered ones; one run at a time

outcome.extras: Itemator's rules on the diff from the fixture to the agent's edits, against the issue text
outcome.recurred: an extra of a test run whose name matches a name answered `remove` in that project's log; names compare as PyPI compares packages (case and runs of - _ . ignored)
outcome.primary: runs with at least one recurred extra, in each arm (of 20)
secondary: recurred extras and all extras per arm
the issue's check per arm: pass, fail, or needs_package (the change imports a package not installed here)

decision.rule: holds if the without arm has at least 5 runs with a recurred extra and the with arm has at most half as many; does_not_hold if the without arm has at least 5 and the with arm more than half; too_few_to_tell if the without arm has fewer than 5

we_report_whatever_happens: both arms' counts in full, every run's diff in results/agent_log_runs/
a check pass rate that drops in the with arm, if it does
a too_few_to_tell result as it is
we_never: rerun a run, or drop one, after seeing its result (a run that crashes before writing anything is rerun once and the crash is reported)
edit the prompt, fixtures, issues or log rule after the first run
claim more than these two projects, this one agent model and these issues
what_we_would_claim: With the answer log, this agent re-added an extra a reviewer had answered `remove` in X of 20 runs, against Y of 20 without it, on two small projects the entrant wrote; the reviewer answers were the entrant's, standing in. Nothing about other agents, real reviewers or other projects.
credits: none: no GitLab Duo run; the agents are Claude Code subagents
